name: 8bit_sciences

subject_rules: one continuous 2D pixel-art SIDE CROSS-SECTION of the body (skin layers), flat side view, no camera move until the final zoom-out

layers top to bottom: air/shoe or object, epidermis (cream bricks), dermis (pink cells with dots), papillary wave, capillaries (thin red vertical), blood-vessel band (dark red), muscle/fat (pink wavy lines)
process shown by tiny pixel actors: fluid, white immune cells with dark nucleus, droplets
materials: hard-edged pixel art, no anti-aliasing, 1 art pixel = 4-6 screen px
look.camera: locked side view; one hard zoom-out to whole limb (e7) then outdoor pixel scene (e8)
look.finish: retro game / 8-bit, CRT scanline + glitch band on every transition

palette_note: measured: pink #C67579 50.1 %, bg #121115 38.1 %, cream #E5CEA9 11.8 %; outdoor end scene adds sky blue + tree green

cut_rhythm.note: one continuous scene; changes are in-scene time jumps (DAY counter) not cuts; one final scene swap at ~22.7 s

motion.real_animation: pixel sprites animate every frame (fluid fills, cells drift, skin bulges); NOT zoom on stills

ui.day_counter: top-left, fast-forward icon (double triangle) + 'DAY n' in small pixel font, white, y~0.035; n updates on each time jump (DAY 1, DAY 2, DAY 5)
ui.callout: single thin line from a structure to a pixel label in capitals (e.g. 'BLISTER'), appears ~0.3 s after the thing forms
ui.transition: CRT scanline overlay + horizontal glitch band, ~0.3 s

script.shape: silent explainer: cause -> damage -> body response (fluid, immune cells) -> time jumps -> healed -> real-life scene

voice.expressiveness: n/a; one short 'Hmm' (speech_ratio 0.026), pitch median 156.7 Hz
voice.note: voice is a sting, not narration

sound.genre: judged: light chiptune / lo-fi game loop, steady 4/4
